notes: One handwritten English letter page on printed Harvard University stationery, dated Aug 4, 1969 and addressed Dear Grothendieck. The printed address includes Cambridge, Massachusetts 02138 and Department of Mathematics, 2 Divinity Avenue. A pencil note at upper right reads Faire copie / pour Jouanolou inside a broken rectangular frame; a pencil vertical stroke marks the quoted-title continuation. An isolated dark mark by the date and a colon-like pair beside pro-A are also preserved. The letter quotes the title Exposé V. Systèmes projectifs J-adiques, par J.P. Jouanolou, asks which seminar it belongs to and whether a newer edition exists, and qualifies the seminar attribution with I suppose. The writer explicitly says the proof of the Theorem of Shih (A.3.1, p. 46) is not understood, says the p. 45 lemma seems valid only for r>p, and calls the equivalence of (i) and (ii) unclear while agreeing with the weaker parenthetical resp. statement. The writer says this casts doubt on A.3.2, p. 47, and Prop. 5.3.1, p. 40, and proposes that working throughout in pro-A with the usual equivalence would remove the difficulty compared with the finer category P_AR. The final two paragraphs ask about biregularity for a finite filtration and propose n and n+1 in place of n and n-1. These are the author's claims and questions; no proof has been checked. Two cancellations are preserved. There is no visible author signature, closing, or manuscript page number on this scan. The lower-left 53 is archive pagination and appears only as a TeX comment. One page was read; H supplies a description only, so it was unavailable for textual collation and all h_reading values are null with diff_h false. Hands remain unnamed because this sheet alone has no signature. No other page or reader output was consulted.
math_reading_decisions: The V in the quoted title has both upper and lower rules and remains a single ordinary Roman numeral.
Both EGA rounded characters are graphically ambiguous between 0 and O. The first receives \unsure{0|O}; the second uses 0 under the recurring-glyph convention.
Both EGA III subscripts have three separately inspected uprights with an upper and a lower rule.
The inequality is r>p: the angle points right. The statement labels are lower-case (i) and (ii).
The two 5 digits in 13.5.5.2 were read separately from their top bars and lower bowls. The second reference reads 11.1.10.
The pro-A capital is an ordinary A; the final P has both A and R in a lower index, with no prime, exclamation mark or doubled capital.
The first line indicator visibly has a point above its minus, represented by \dot{-}1; the second has a plain -1.
The final index condition is n and n+1, instead of n and n-1, with a real crossing upright in the plus sign.
